construct: The second pharyngeal arch overgrows the third and fourth arches, creating a transient cervical sinus lined by ectoderm. Failure of complete obliteration can leave a second branchial cleft cyst, sinus, or fistula; the cyst classically lies along the anterior border of the sternocleidomastoid.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: A painless lateral neck mass along the anterior SCM that does not move with tongue protrusion is a second branchial cleft cyst from persistent cervical sinus tissue.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: A thyroglossal duct cyst is common in young patients but is usually midline and moves with swallowing or tongue protrusion.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Location and movement behavior separate persistent cervical sinus from thyroglossal and other embryologic remnants.
